title: Impact rhythm planning scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal cadence plan to keep my quarterly objectives honest and tied to measurable micro-actions.
- Not trying to ship org OKRs here — this is the lightweight mechanism I use to keep momentum across weeks where meetings and fires distract me.

Quarter objective (Q4-ish draft):
- O: Build a predictable weekly rhythm that increases measurable impact on three priorities: (1) Model latency experiments, (2) Routing policy docs, (3) Customer debugging time reduction.
  - Why: I drift between deep work and firefighting; having a compact, repeatable cadence will increase continuity for experiments and reduce context-switch cost.

Key results (proto, measurable):
- KR1: 6 repeatable micro-experiments completed and logged with before/after latency and cost delta (target: >=3 showing >=5% improvement).
- KR2: Reduce average time-to-first-debug (from customer-reported issue to root-cause) from 48h to 30h for my assigned tickets (sample n>=10).
- KR3: Ship 1 reference doc for routing policy decision-tree and get 2 teams to adopt/copy it.

Weekly structure (my lightweight ritual):
- Monday morning (30m): Set 3 priority micro-tasks (one for each priority). Quick plan: what success looks like by Friday.
- Wed mid-day (15m): Signal check — metric snapshot and one-line blocker list.
- Friday afternoon (45m): Capture results, lessons, and one experiment to carry forward.
- Note to self: Block these slots in calendar as "Impact Rhythm" (do not auto-cancel).

Micro-experiment template (keep short):
- Hypothesis (1 line): e.g., "Switching to fused kernel A will reduce 512-token p50 by >4% for model-x."
- Test plan (2–4 bullets): dataset, request pattern, metric(s).
- Run (time/date):
- Results (numbers): baseline -> variant -> delta -> confidence (low/med/high).
- Quick conclusion: next action (rollout / revert / iterate).

Metrics / quick dashboard I care about (snapshot each Wed):
- p50 latency (ms) for my experiments (last 7 days)
- per-token cost estimate ($) for top 3 configs
- Mean time to first debug (tickets assigned)
- # experiments with positive delta / total experiments

Check-in template (Friday):
- Wins: (3 bullets)
- Misses / surprises: (2 bullets)
- Decision: continue / stop / escalate (one line per experiment)
- What I learned: (single-sentence insight)
- Carryover experiment for next week: (name + short reason)

Recent entries (working notes):
- 2024-11-12: Kickoff — created cadence, added calendar blocks for Mon/Wed/Fri.
- 2024-11-19: Exp-512-kernel-A: baseline p50=420ms -> variant=402ms (-4.3%). Confidence: med. Next: run with 95th perc scenario and check memory.
- 2024-11-22: Debug-time sample (tickets 1121, 1168, 1190): avg=50h -> identified common missing logs -> propose small logging shim to reduce triage. If approved, expect drop to ~30h.
- 2024-11-29: Routing doc skeleton drafted (initial decision tree + example routes). Need peer review from Arjun. Goal: get two teams to copy by Jan.

Retrospective notes (end of month):
- What worked: timeboxing experiments forced me to finish runs instead of leaving half-done.
- What didn't: I under-estimated data-analysis time (cleaning logs), so experiments pile up.
- Adjustments: add a 60m "analysis sprint" twice per month to clear backlog. Also create small parsing scripts to standardize metrics export.

Open questions / blockers to resolve:
- Do we have an internal standard metric definition for "time-to-first-debug"? If not, propose v1: time between ticket creation and first successful reproduction or initial triage comment. Link to propose: CONFLUENCE-PT-279.
- Who can help approve the logging shim? (Ping: @Arjun for prioritization).
- Does infra team want me to run bigger kernel tests on dedicated pool or use shared queue? Cost/priority tradeoff. JIRA:ENG-2789 notes this.

Immediate todos (this week):
- [ ] Convert Exp-512-kernel-A runs into reproducible script and push PR (github.com/redwood-inference/pr/421).
- [ ] Draft quick proposal for logging shim and add to my 1:1 agenda with Dev Manager.
- [ ] Peer review routing doc with Arjun and Sophie; add example for canary policy.

Notes to self (style/habits):
- Keep experiment scope small (aim 2–4h per run including quick analysis).
- Close the loop: if an experiment fails, write a one-line reason and move on; don't perfect that analysis.
- Share Friday wins in #team-weekly-signal to create social pressure for continuity.

Archive / references:
- Saved experiment templates: drive:personal/exp-templates/2024
- Quick snippets (bash/python) for metrics export: snippets/metrics-utils.gist

End-of-doc scribbles (brain dump):
- If I can create a 2x reduction in time-to-debug for a few customer-facing tickets, that's high leverage (less context switching, happier customers).
- If routing doc reduces unnecessary high-cost model calls by a few percent, cost savings compound across customer usage.
- Consider pairing with Solutions Eng for one customer deep-dive next month.
